findings.title: Foundational measurements and cited artifacts are absent from this working tree
findings.description:
The design states "Probed against this repo's real graph (v2.8.1, `gitCommitHash` `1bfbca1`, 925 nodes / 2184 edges / 10 layers / 15 tour steps) while writing this design. These are measurements, not assumptions, and the design's decisions rest on them." None of the three things this rests on are present in the repository as checked out:

- `.understand-anything/` does not exist at the repo root (and `.gitignore` has no `understand`/`trash` entry, so it would be tracked if present). Slice 361's own task file records this explicitly at `project-documents/user/tasks/361-tasks.graph-contract-and-provenance.md:39`: "**`.understand-anything/` does not exist in this repo** — Task 0.1 is a hard prerequisite for every walkthrough task," and the architecture's "Current State" says the same.
- `commands/analysis/understand.md` — the file the Overview calls "the existing" one and the only file this slice edits — does not exist; `commands/analysis/` contains only `tech-debt-audit.md`.
- The "generated `943` sample" (line 136, line 368, line 466) does not exist: `project-documents/user/analysis/` holds only `940`/`941`/`942` tech-debt-audit runs. Slice 361's frontmatter still reads `status: not_started`, and the DEVLOG's 20260818 entries end at "Next: Phase 6 implementation" for 361 — there is no 361 implementation-complete entry.

The design's own guard in walkthrough step 1 only covers "if these three numbers do not agree" — it does not cover "the file is not there," which is the state an implementer starting from this document would hit first. The design should state the prerequisite plainly (361 implemented, plus its PM-gated Task 0.1 graph generation) and add an explicit stop branch to walkthrough step 1 for absent graph / absent `understand.md`, in the same spirit as the existing stop-and-report instruction. As written, "Everything here is markdown edits to the existing `commands/analysis/understand.md`" (line 22) asserts a starting state that does not hold.

findings.title: Correction 1 attributes text to the 361 contract that neither 361 artifact contains
findings.description:
The design's justification for its first correction is "The 361 skill states that `nodeIds` mixes file, function, and class nodes and instructs intersecting with `type == "file"` to get a file count." I could not find that statement in either 361 artifact. `project-documents/user/slices/361-slice.graph-contract-and-provenance.md` contains exactly one type selector, at line 108 — `.nodes[] | select(.type == "file" or ...)` — which is a node selector, not a layer `nodeIds` intersection; and its layer instruction at line 297 is "each layer's name, description, and file count, from `layers[]`" with no intersect step. The task file matches (lines 117-119, 297). So the offending text is either in the unimplemented skill file or the attribution is wrong.

This matters because the correction is the reason the design calls itself "not merely additive" and the reason 364's layer-boundary derivations are claimed to be fixed. If the premise is not where the design says it is, the implementer cannot locate the text to change. Either cite the specific section/line of the implemented `commands/analysis/understand.md` that carries the offending instruction, or drop the correction to whatever text actually exists. I am not asserting the text is absent from the eventual implementation — only that neither artifact under review contains it, so the premise is unverified.

findings.title: Correction 2 defines "file-level" three ways and the selector matches none of them cleanly
findings.description:
Within one subsection the term gets three definitions: the heading says "file-level" means "carries a `filePath`"; the prose says "the file-level selector becomes an explicit type allow-list"; the code is a type exclusion, `select(.type != "function" and .type != "class")`; and the parent architecture's definition is a named set of nine types (`file`, `config`, `service`, `endpoint`, `schema`, `table`, `pipeline`, `document`, `resource`). The sentence "the file-level selector becomes an explicit type allow-list, and the two excluded types ... stay excluded by name" is internally contradictory — it announces an allow-list and then specifies an exclusion.

The stated definition ("carries a `filePath`") is not what the mechanism implements; `select(.filePath != null)` would express the definition directly and, on the measured graph, yields the same 238. The architecture's own framing is the nine-type enumeration, so "aligned with the architecture" means the allow-list, not the exclusion. The design's future-proofing rationale for the exclusion is reasonable, but it should be argued as a deliberate, named deviation from the architecture's enumeration rather than presented as the architecture's definition. Pick one definition, make the selector express it, and say which one the architecture sanctions.

A related measurement-scope mismatch in the same area: the "Verified graph facts" row states `tags` coverage as "201/201" — file nodes only — while section 3's selector operates over "file-level `nodes[]`" (238 under the corrected definition), and the "27" entry-point count is therefore measured over a narrower population than the section that consumes it. Either state the count over 238 or state that config/pipeline nodes carry no tags.

findings.title: Section 7's absence rules for the new non-graph read are self-contradictory and its failure modes are incomplete
findings.description:
`.understandignore` is the one genuinely new I/O path — the design says so itself ("The one new read that is not a `jq` selection against the graph is `.understandignore`"), which makes its failure handling mandatory rather than optional. Section 7 gives it one sentence and the sentence contradicts itself:

> "An all-comments file (this repo's current state has 17 active lines) is reported as "defaults only", not as a gap."

An all-comments file has zero active lines; the parenthetical asserts 17 active lines for this repo's file. The two halves describe different states and the design does not say which rule applies to this repo's actual file — the very file the walkthrough's spot-check counts (`grep -vE '^\s*(#|$)' .understandignore | wc -l`). "Defaults only" is also undefined: no upstream default ignore set is established anywhere in the architecture or this design, so an implementer cannot know what is being reported.

The failure modes for the three new file reads are also uneven. The mapping row's fallback is "`[GAP: ...]` naming the unreadable file," which covers unreadable but not absent; the walkthrough covers absent `meta.json` only. And for `config.json` the prose says "Do not report an absent optional setting as a gap," which an implementer can reasonably read as "do not report an absent `config.json`" — the opposite of what the fallback column requires. Enumerate the states explicitly for each of the three files (absent / present-but-unreadable / present-and-empty) and give each one outcome.

findings.title: `[INFERRED]` governance bans inference while requiring a per-section interpretive sentence
findings.description:
The decision — "`[INFERRED]` is defined but not used by this flow, and its use is a defect here" — is well aligned with the architecture's "Never fabricate intent" and "Derive, never invent." But the section then carves out an exception that reintroduces exactly what it bans: "The one apparent exception is the closing observation each section carries — the sentence that reads a pattern out of the data ('complexity concentrates in the seams where squadron meets an external SDK')."

This is a new mechanism the architecture does not ask for: nothing in the parent architecture's comprehension outputs or the slice plan entry for 362 requests a closing interpretive sentence per section. It also sits in direct tension with the binding rule two sections earlier — "A section is never ... filled with prose that is not traceable to its named fields" — and with Success Criteria 2's "never inferred prose." The design's safeguard is "the test is mechanical: if the sentence is not derivable from the table directly above it, it does not belong," but "derivable from the table" is a judgment call, not a mechanical test, and a sentence that "reads a pattern out of the data" is precisely the category the architecture treats as intent rather than structure.

The lighter option is to cut the requirement: the seven sourced sections already deliver the developer value the slice plan states. If the closing sentence stays, it needs a check an implementer can actually apply (for example, a sentence that introduces no noun or adjective absent from the section's own table), and it should be stated as added scope with a reason rather than as an exception to the rule it contradicts.

findings.title: Two interface fields are read and measured but consumed by no section
findings.description: `edges[].direction` is listed under Interfaces Required as "Dependency ordering," but mapping row 6 orders by "descending count, ties by `weight`" and never uses direction. `tour[].languageLesson` is measured in the facts table (9/15 populated) and appears in no section. Neither is expensive, but both are scope the design carries without a consumer — cut them from the interface table and the facts table, or name the section that uses them.

findings.title: Scope statement contradicts itself on whether the retained reference document is edited
findings.description: The Overview says "Everything here is markdown edits to the existing `commands/analysis/understand.md`," and the Technical Scope's Included list does not mention a second file. But Success Criteria 11 and Implementation Notes step 5 both change `user/reference/analyze-codebase-prompt.md`. The `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` reuse section compounds it: "the document stays in `user/reference/` unchanged" followed by "A one-line note is added to it." The parent architecture permits the cross-reference (it retains the document as a low-cost alternative path and does not supersede it), but the slice's own scope statements should agree on whether it is one changed file or two.

findings.title: The extraction mapping is fully traceable to architecture-named fields with no third outcome
findings.description: All seven sections source from fields the parent architecture's output contract and Capability 1 flow actually name: `project` and file-level nodes with `summary`/`filePath`/`complexity` (Flow step 3), `layers[]` and `tour[]` (Flow step 3), `edges[]` (output contract), `meta.json`/`config.json`/`.understandignore` (output contract table, which explicitly authorizes `.understandignore` "when explaining coverage gaps"). The architecture's required comprehension outputs — layers, complexity hotspots, entry points, dependency observations — are all present, and the three additions are additions to the same named field set rather than new sources. The fallback column's "no third option" rule is a faithful per-section application of the architecture's "Every field resolves to exactly one of: content derived from its named source, or a gap marker ... There is no third outcome in which the skill supplies the content itself," and the fallbacks that delegate to preflight (rows 2, 6, and `project` in row 1) match 361's stated rejection behavior rather than restating it differently. Gap-marker syntax matches the `[GAP: {what is missing} — {which input would supply it}]` form settled in 361.

findings.title: Both parent open questions are settled in the assigned slice, and the prior sample is preserved
findings.description:
The parent architecture's two open questions are "Reuse of `analyze-codebase-prompt.md`" and "Gap-marker syntax," and the slice plan assigns the former to 362 explicitly ("the `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` reuse question is answered in 362 where its analysis template is the direct comparable"). The design answers it in the architecture's own terms — adopt the fact/inference discipline and the say-so-explicitly rule, adopt no structure, retain the document — and its reasoning (the ten-part template is built for a probe+Repomix backend that supplies CI configs and source text the graph does not) is a substantive comparison rather than a deferral. The `[INFERRED]` decision is recorded as a decision with a stated governance owner for 363's use, which is what the slice plan asks for.

The instruction to leave the 943 sample in place and unedited also respects the architecture's "each run is an independent sample rather than a revision of the last," and correctly refuses to retroactively rewrite a generated artifact — which is the right call for a design whose corrections change what future runs produce.
